description: Agent Cybersecurity: submit a vendor’s security evidence with the buyer’s review policy: the vendor with its name and the service it provides; the policy with the days within which evidence must be dated, the hours within which a breach must be told and its text; each piece of evidence with its id, kind (SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 1, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, an equivalent attestation, a penetration test, a questionnaire or other), the days it was issued, its period ended and it expires, whether its scope covers the service used and the exceptions it notes; the sub-processor list with its names and the day it was updated; the agreement with the hours it allows to tell of a breach and its text; and optionally the day the evidence is read on. The signed report gives the vendor, the policy, the evidence supplied with the attestations current inside the review cycle and whether one covers a period, the sub-processor list with its date and age, the breach-notice hours in the agreement against the policy, and the evidence outside the cycle, and counts them, and names undocumented evidence: no SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS or equivalent attestation, no attestation current inside the review cycle, and an agreement with no breach-notice term; then a breach-notice term longer than the policy allows, a current attestation that is only a point-in-time SOC 2 Type 1 report, a current attestation whose scope does not cover the service used, exceptions the attestation notes and a sub-processor list outside the review cycle or undated, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No review cycle, no evidence, no sub-processor list, no agreement, no breach-notice limit in the policy, no day read on or an attestation with no date leaves the evidence unverified. This reads whether the vendor’s whole security evidence file is current against the buyer’s policy: wever_audit-evidence-check reads one audit report’s scope, opinion and exceptions, wever_subprocessor-evidence-check pairs sub-processor claims against a list, wever_dpa-evidence-check reads a data processing agreement’s clauses and wever_certification-evidence-check reads certification claims against evidence. Verdict cyber_vendor_undocumented, cyber_vendor_partial, cyber_vendor_unverified or cyber_vendor_documented. POST /api/cyber-vendor-check. Reads the security records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment, system scan, probe or external write. Agent Cybersecurity reads an organization’s own security records after the fact and checks them against the stated policy and against themselves: standing access, the secrets inventory, the component and patch record, the exported configuration, logging coverage, backup and restore evidence, a vendor’s security evidence and incident readiness. Beside it, the Agent Risk checks such as wever_risk-exposure-check read one planned action’s worst case and limits before it runs, while a cyber check reads security posture from the records; and the security reads elsewhere in the catalog keep their families, each named beside the check it meets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-cybersecurity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-cybersecurity/.

evidence.description: Each piece of security evidence, as supplied.

covers_service.description: Whether its scope covers the service used.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.
